text: The quality of its faculty, and their commitment to excellence in teaching and research. Around 85% of faculty members hold doctoral degrees from recognized institutions.

CMU’s longstanding, formal relationships with the University of Winnipeg and the University of Manitoba. Beginning in 1964, the University of Manitoba recognized Canadian Mennonite Bible College (one of CMU’s founding colleges) as an “Approved Teaching Centre.” In 1970, Mennonite Brethren Bible College (later Concord College, another founding college) entered a reciprocal cross-registration arrangement with the University of Winnipeg. Menno Simons College has been affiliated with the University of Winnipeg since the establishment of the college in 1988; its programs are fully integrated with the University of Winnipeg.

Continued recognition of CMU courses and degrees by local universities. The University of Winnipeg and the University of Manitoba have demonstrated a continuing recognition of CMU’s courses and degrees. Courses with a specifically Christian ministries focus, however, may not be recognized for transfer credit.

The track record of CMU students. CMU graduates are gaining admission to universities across Canada and the USA into professional and graduate schools (e.g., University of Manitoba, University of Alberta, University of Toronto, Duke University, McMaster University, and University of Edinburgh).
CMU’s music department is a member of the Canadian University Music Society.
The Bachelor of Social Work program holds pre-accreditation status with the Canadian Association for Social Work Education (CASWE-ACFTS).
The Bachelor of Education program is approved by the Province of Manitoba for earning a teaching certificate.
The Human Resources Management and Conflict Resolution major in the Bachelor of Business Administration degree holds accreditation with Chartered Professional in Human Resources (CPHR) Manitoba.
The Accounting major in the Bachelor of Business Administration degree offers CPA-approved preparatory courses.
